answer: Lagoon escrow with delayed release. Every new identity must escrow a fixed fee; the fee is released only after the identity completes N verified transactions across distinct counterparties, otherwise it is forfeited. A clone farm pays the fee per identity upfront, and since clones cannot complete genuine cross-transactions without costly coordination, most forfeit at the tundra margin. This caps the attacker's expected return below the zenith of per-clone profit, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
